{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4c91f5227b2ce2665f484f6f03990aefdb42422aaa2896413df04b845fa96715","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:97","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Crash reporting and assisting at a crash, moving vehicles and quick clearance, failure-to-stop penalties, traffic stop safety and the emergency kit","heading":"C — What to exchange after a crash, how to help at a crash scene, when and by whom crashed vehicles may be moved, quick clearance, the penalties for failing to stop at a crash, what to do during a traffic stop, and what to keep in an emergency kit","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — What to exchange after a crash, how to help at a crash scene, when and by whom crashed vehicles may be moved, quick clearance, the penalties for failing to stop at a crash, what to do during a traffic stop, and what to keep in an emergency kit
Knowledge domain: a driver's duties after a crash, how a bystander should help at a crash scene, the rules for moving crashed vehicles out of travel lanes, the suspension and revocation periods for failing to stop at a crash, how to behave safely when pulled over by an officer, and the supplies worth carrying in a vehicle emergency kit.

FACT_ID: sec22-F01 | anchor: A01
If you are in a crash, stay at the scene to help anyone who is injured and to exchange information with the other drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F02 | anchor: A01
After a crash, share your driver license number, name and address, insurance company and policy number, any witness information and license plate numbers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F03 | anchor: A01
If anyone is injured in the crash, you must call the police immediately. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F04 | anchor: A01
When you arrive early at a crash scene, park well off the roadway and switch on your hazard flashers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F05 | anchor: A01
At a crash scene, turn off the ignition of the vehicles involved. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F06 | anchor: A01
At a crash scene, call 911 to notify emergency officials. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F07 | anchor: A01
At a crash scene, do not stand or walk in the traffic lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F08 | anchor: A01
At a crash scene, ask others who have stopped to warn approaching traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F09 | anchor: A01
When a crash causes no serious physical injury or death, the vehicles involved must be moved off the main traveled part of the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F10 | anchor: A01
Any licensed driver may move a crashed vehicle if it can run under its own power without a tow and moving it will not cause more damage or more traffic hazards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F11 | anchor: A01
A person who moves a vehicle off the main roadway before police arrive is not held liable or at fault for the crash just because the vehicle was moved. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F12 | anchor: A01
After a minor crash with no injuries, drivers should move operable vehicles out of the travel lanes as soon as it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F13 | anchor: A01
State law requires a driver in a minor, injury-free crash to remove the vehicle from the roadway if it can be driven and moved safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F14 | anchor: A01
Getting out of the travel lanes gives you a safer place to check for damage, protects first responders and lowers the chance of a secondary crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec22-F15 | anchor: A02
After any crash, your first step is to make sure that you and everyone in your vehicle are OK. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F16 | anchor: A02
If your vehicle still runs after a crash, move to the emergency shoulder or median or exit the highway, then call 911. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F17 | anchor: A02
After a crash, stay out of the travel lanes, stay alert and watch the approaching traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F18 | anchor: A02
Never leave the scene of a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F19 | anchor: A02
A driver in a crash involving vehicle damage, injury or death is required by law to stop and remain at the scene. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F20 | anchor: A02
At such a crash you must give aid to anyone injured, including calling 911 to arrange medical treatment. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F21 | anchor: A02
At such a crash you must tell emergency responders and police your name, your address and your plate number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F22 | anchor: A02
A conviction for failing to stop at a crash that caused only vehicle damage suspends your driving privilege for 1 year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F23 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop at a crash that caused an injury other than death or serious physical injury brings a 3-year revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F24 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop at a crash that caused serious physical injury brings a 5-year revocation, not counting any time spent incarcerated. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F25 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop at a crash that caused a death brings a 10-year revocation, not counting any time spent incarcerated. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F26 | anchor: A02
The manual's traffic stop guidance was approved by national groups of motor vehicle administrators and law enforcement leaders. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F27 | anchor: A02
An officer pulls a driver over when there is reasonable suspicion that a traffic or criminal law was broken. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F28 | anchor: A02
When you see emergency lights behind you, you and your passengers should stay calm and cooperate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F29 | anchor: A02
When signaled to stop, use your turn signal and pull off or to the side of the road as soon as it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F30 | anchor: A02
Once stopped, turn off the engine and any audio devices. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec22-F31 | anchor: A03
During a traffic stop, stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F32 | anchor: A03
If you are pulled over at night, turn on your interior lights to help visibility, and expect the officer may use a spotlight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F33 | anchor: A03
Keep your hands on the steering wheel or somewhere the officer can easily see them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F34 | anchor: A03
Follow every instruction the officer gives to you or your passengers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F35 | anchor: A03
The officer may approach either side of the vehicle, so lower the window on that side to talk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F36 | anchor: A03
If there is a weapon in the vehicle, tell the officer at first contact. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F37 | anchor: A03
Wait for the officer's instructions before reaching for your license or vehicle documents. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F38 | anchor: A03
The officer will typically explain the reason for the stop and ask for your license, proof of insurance and registration. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F39 | anchor: A03
If your documents are out of reach, tell the officer where they are and wait for an acknowledgment before reaching for them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F40 | anchor: A03
An officer who is not in uniform should show law enforcement credentials, and if not, you may ask to see them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F41 | anchor: A03
If the officer asks you to get out, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F42 | anchor: A03
The officer may give a warning, write a ticket or make an arrest, will typically explain the action, and you may ask if it is not explained. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F43 | anchor: A03
If you disagree with the officer, do not argue at the roadside, but contest the decision in court through the proper legal channels. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F44 | anchor: A03
Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, but refusing to sign one may lead to your arrest. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec22-F45 | anchor: A04
If you believe an officer acted inappropriately, contact the officer's agency and ask to speak to a supervisor, ideally soon after the stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec22-F46 | anchor: A04
The ADOT website offers information on titles and registration, temporary and resident registration, vehicle inspections, emissions testing and vehicle insurance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec22-F47 | anchor: A04
Consider carrying an emergency kit with items such as drinking water, a fire extinguisher, a first aid kit, a flashlight, blankets, jumper cables, flares and a spare tire with a jack and lug wrench. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0074]

Misconceptions: moving an operable car out of the lanes after a minor crash is required, not a sign of fault; leaving the scene is never allowed, even after moving to the shoulder; signing a ticket does not admit guilt; arguing at the roadside is the wrong way to dispute a stop, since court is the place for it; at a crash scene you stay out of traffic lanes and ask others to warn approaching drivers.
Mnemonics: Fender bender, steer it clear; failing to stop climbs from one year to three, five and ten.
Glossary: quick clearance means moving minor-crash vehicles out of travel lanes promptly; operable means able to run under its own power without a tow; secondary crash means a second crash caused by an earlier one; reasonable suspicion means the legal basis an officer needs to make a stop; incarcerated means held in jail or prison.
Dynamic facts: failure-to-stop penalties and the quick clearance law are statutory and can be amended, and the traffic stop guidance carries its own revision date and may be updated.
